packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-15 - unverified first reading from images only

Exposure / method notes
- No identification of the work or author was revealed to me. The images themselves show modern shelfmark-type labels ("Stams, StA, ..." on the paper mount in image-003; pencil "STA, Fragm. 64..." on the parchment in image-002 and image-004; "../61" and "1666/6" low on image-004). The directory name also contains "stams". These are provenance labels, not identifications of the text, and I did not use them.
- Beyond the rules: to inspect detail I made 2x enlarged crops of image-002 and image-004 in my own scratch directory with PIL. I read only those derived crops and the four packet images. Nothing else.
- All four images loaded.

Layout survey (observations)
- image-001: overview of one face (reduced). A small fragment cut into four vertical strips, held together at the bottom by a clear plastic sleeve. A paper mount beside it is masked by a grey rectangle.
- image-002: native-resolution view of the same face (I call it face A). image-003: overview of the other face. image-004: native view of that face (face B). There are no separate overlapping tiles. Each native image shows a whole face.
- Two-column layout, ruled, Gothic textualis book hand in brown ink, with red used for one initial and one rubric. On face A the leftmost strip carries line-ends of one column (col. a), followed by the intercolumn space with a vertical ruling. The other three strips carry the beginnings and middles of the second column (col. b). Face B is the mirror image. Its leftmost strip carries middles of col. a lines. Strips 2-3 carry later parts of the same col. a lines. The rightmost strip carries line-beginnings of col. b.
- The strips are separated by vertical cuts, and the two narrow middle pieces are wrinkled and abraded. Letters at the strip edges are lost. On each face roughly a third to a half of each line survives in col. b, and only 4-9 letters per line survive in the col. a fragment.
- Face A has a red two-line initial (C?) at the col. b line beginning near the bottom, and one line in red (a rubric) just above it. Face B has red touches on an initial Q (line 2) and on an initial A (line 10, col. b).
- Tentative: col. b on face A looks like narrative or expository prose that cites authorities by name (visible: "historia ecclesiastica", "Beda", "magister Johannes Beleth"). A feast-related rubric follows. I am not identifying the work.

Selected spans
- Face A, col. b: all 14 surviving lines read as far as possible. Face A, col. a: line-ends.
- Face B, col. a (middles) and col. b (beginnings): all lines attempted.
- Unread: everything beyond the cut strip edges, and the badly abraded narrow middle strips. A view with raking light or UV might recover the narrow strips.
Conventions: " | " marks a physical gap or strip cut within the line. [..] marks lost or illegible letters at a cut. Expansions are in ( ). "?" follows an uncertain reading.

Limitations
- Only narrow vertical strips survive. No line is complete, and nothing joins across the strip cuts, so I have not filled anything in.
- The two narrow middle strips on both faces are wrinkled and rubbed. Letters there are guesses at best.
- Line correspondence between face A col. a and col. b assumes the ruling runs straight across, which it appears to do.
- The red rubric on face A l.13 is mostly faded. A colour-enhanced or UV image would be the most useful next view.
